title: Role sessions (coordinator, batch runner, triage and the rest) fan work out to agents and run it in parallel, and drop nothing they could multitask
why:
Owner complaint, 00:17 CST Nov 15 (typed to the consultant, relayed 00:24 CST; verbatim): "also none of the role sessions like coordinator batchrunner triage etc are using subagents effectively… why?? they rarely delegate or act in parallel and they often drop sruff when they cud be multitasking". Why it matters: the owner judges the work by how fast and how complete it lands (his goal, 20:17 CST Nov 14: max efficiency, no waste, accurate, fastest). Plan: the coordinator first runs a 12 h audit of Agent use per role session (how many Agent or fork calls each role made, which items each dropped or did one after another when they could have run in parallel); the audit reads transcripts or session events, and no number is stated before it is read. The fix follows the audit, not before it. Rules the audit measures against (read in the loaded CLAUDE.md): roles-orchestrator-never-builds (a spawner plans, briefs, verifies and reports; builds only a bounded change), parallelism-keep-going (when a lane ends, start each queued item whose questions are answered, in the same turn), parallelism-own-lane-orchestrator and parallelism-each-own-checkout (fan out, each in its own checkout). Earlier owner word on the same point, to triage: "send subagents like delegate responsibilities man" (Nov 14); triage has since given each filing, check and sort to a background fork. That is evidence of one role's change, not proof that the fix works; the audit says. Related: step role-model-explore-veto-offer, ruled-step-coordinator-queue. Not read by triage: any role session's Agent-call counts.
